baseline: socket01 asserts a 9-row (domain,type,protocol)->(retval,errno) table over socket(2). Host LTP 20260529 binary: 9 passed / 0 failed / 0 broken. Per row, what the correct kernel returns (each independently re-measured on this container's Linux 6.8.0-124 with /tmp/sockprobe.c): tdat[0] (0=AF_UNSPEC, SOCK_STREAM, 0) -> -1/EAFNOSUPPORT(97); tdat[1] (AF_INET, 75, 0) -> -1/EINVAL(22); tdat[2] (AF_UNIX, SOCK_DGRAM, 0) -> fd; tdat[3] (AF_INET, SOCK_RAW, 0) -> -1/EPROTONOSUPPORT(93); tdat[4] (AF_INET, SOCK_DGRAM, 17) -> fd; tdat[5] (AF_INET, SOCK_STREAM, 17) -> -1/EPROTONOSUPPORT(93); tdat[6] (AF_INET, SOCK_DGRAM, 6) -> -1/EPROTONOSUPPORT(93); tdat[7] (AF_INET, SOCK_STREAM, 6) -> fd; tdat[8] (AF_INET, SOCK_STREAM, 1) -> -1/EPROTONOSUPPORT(93). Correction to the case name: tdat[3] is labelled 'raw open as non-root' but the errno is capability-independent -- measured as root with full CAP_NET_RAW it is still EPROTONOSUPPORT, because protocol 0 on SOCK_RAW is a wildcard request with no default raw protocol to resolve to, and the permission check only runs after the protocol lookup succeeds. Proof it is not a privilege answer: socket(AF_INET,SOCK_RAW,1) and socket(AF_INET,SOCK_RAW,255) both succeed as root. So no fix may return EPERM here.
failing_assertion: socket01.c:67, four times, all identical: 'TFAIL: expected EPROTONOSUPPORT(93): EAFNOSUPPORT (97)'. Asterinas scores 5 passed / 4 failed / 0 broken in 0.013s. The four are exactly tdat[3] 'raw open as non-root', tdat[5] 'UDP stream', tdat[6] 'TCP dgram' and tdat[8] 'ICMP stream'; every one returns -1 with EAFNOSUPPORT(97) where EPROTONOSUPPORT(93) is required. tdat[0], [1], [2], [4] and [7] already pass. (Per-case lines are not in qemu.log by default -- kirk prints only 'socket01: fail'; they were captured by temporarily forcing KIRK_VERBOSE=1 in test/initramfs/src/conformance/ltp/run_ltp_test.sh, which has been reverted.)
root_cause: sys_socket decides the whole (family, type, protocol) triple in one inline match at lines 28-94, and every rejection arm in it returns EAFNOSUPPORT regardless of which of the three arguments was actually at fault. Three specific arms produce the four failures. (a) Line 50, the AF_INET|AF_INET6 + SOCK_STREAM arm: Protocol::try_from(17) and (1) succeed (both are Protocol enum variants), the inner match accepts only IPPROTO_IP|IPPROTO_TCP, so protocol 17 and protocol 1 fall to '_ => EAFNOSUPPORT, "unsupported protocol"' -- tdat[5] and tdat[8]. (b) Line 60, the AF_INET + SOCK_DGRAM arm: same shape, accepts only IPPROTO_IP|IPPROTO_UDP, so protocol 6 hits '_ => EAFNOSUPPORT, "unsupported protocol"' -- tdat[6]. Note both arms have already recognised the family, so EAFNOSUPPORT is self-contradictory: the message says 'unsupported protocol' while the errno says the address family is unsupported. (c) Line 93, the outer '_ => EAFNOSUPPORT, "unsupported domain"': there is no (AF_INET, SOCK_RAW) arm at all, so tdat[3] falls all the way through to the domain catch-all even though AF_INET is fully supported. The failure is purely the errno constant selected -- no argument conversion is rejected, no allocation is attempted, and socket() only allocates an fd, so nothing here needs a network device. Confirming the constant is simply absent: EPROTONOSUPPORT is defined at kernel/src/error.rs:110 and ESOCKTNOSUPPORT at :111, but grep finds zero uses of either anywhere under kernel/src -- while EAFNOSUPPORT is returned from 11 sites, 6 of them in this one function.
invariant: socket(2) rejects its three arguments on three distinct axes and each axis owns a different errno, so the errno tells the caller which argument to change. An address family the kernel does not implement is EAFNOSUPPORT. A family that is implemented but has no handler for the requested socket type is ESOCKTNOSUPPORT. A family and type that are both implemented, but whose requested protocol is not one that pair implements -- including protocol 0 when that pair has no default protocol to resolve the wildcard to -- is EPROTONOSUPPORT. The consequence that is violated here: once the family has been recognised, EAFNOSUPPORT must never be returned; any later rejection is about the type or the protocol, not the family. This also fixes the ordering -- the protocol must be resolved before any capability check, so an unresolvable protocol reports EPROTONOSUPPORT rather than EPERM even to an unprivileged caller.
owning_layer: The per-family socket-creation dispatch -- Linux's net_proto_family::create hook (inet_create, unix_create, netlink_create), which is entered once per family and is therefore shared by every caller that creates a socket. Asterinas has no such layer: sys_socket inlines the entire family x type x protocol table into the syscall handler, and sys_socketpair inlines a second, divergent copy of it. The closest equivalent in Asterinas's own design, and where the rule should be enforced, is a family-dispatch constructor under kernel/src/net/socket/ that both sys_socket and sys_socketpair call -- i.e. the family layer, below the syscall layer. Only the family-agnostic checks belong in kernel/src/syscall/socket.rs: the type-range check (SockType::try_from, correctly EINVAL today) and the flag-bit check. Stated as a placement rule: the family/type/protocol errno decision must be made once per family, not once per syscall entry point, or each entry point drifts -- which is already observable, since socket.rs and socketpair.rs disagree today.
linux_reference: Could not be read from source: every code host is blocked from this container (elixir.bootlin.com, raw.githubusercontent.com, sources.debian.org and man7.org all fail with 'Unable to verify if domain is safe to fetch'). Substituted the stronger evidence available here -- this container runs real Linux 6.8.0-124, so the reference behaviour was measured directly rather than inferred (/tmp/sockprobe.c through sockprobe4.c). Where Linux enforces each axis, from that measurement plus the known structure of the call path: net/socket.c __sock_create holds the family-agnostic checks (family out of range or family registered as NULL -> EAFNOSUPPORT; type >= SOCK_MAX -> EINVAL; unknown bits in the type's flag half -> EINVAL, measured: socket(AF_INET, SOCK_STREAM|0x40, 0) -> EINVAL); net/ipv4/af_inet.c inet_create holds the protocol axis in its lookup_protocol loop over inetsw[type], where err starts at -ESOCKTNOSUPPORT so a type with no protosw entry keeps that value (measured: AF_INET+SOCK_RDM -> ESOCKTNOSUPPORT(94)) and becomes -EPROTONOSUPPORT when the loop finds entries but none matches (measured on both AF_INET and AF_INET6 for protocol 1, 17, 6 and 99); net/unix/af_unix.c unix_create holds the same axis for AF_UNIX (measured: AF_UNIX+SOCK_STREAM+protocol 6 -> EPROTONOSUPPORT, protocol 0 and 1 -> ok, matching 'if (protocol && protocol != PF_UNIX)'). The decisive measurement for the layer claim, which does not depend on reading any source: socketpair(AF_INET, SOCK_RAW, 0) returns EPROTONOSUPPORT(93) while socketpair(AF_INET, SOCK_STREAM, 0) returns EOPNOTSUPP(95). Both are the same syscall on the same family, so the EPROTONOSUPPORT can only have come from the family create hook running before the ->socketpair op is consulted -- i.e. Linux enforces this rule strictly below the syscall entry, in a place both socket() and socketpair() traverse. What I could not verify: the exact file/line placement above is prior knowledge corroborated by black-box measurement, not a source read this run.
other_callers: Not 'nobody else' -- the same defect is reachable through five other paths, which is why the layer choice matters more than the three-line edit. (1) sys_socketpair, kernel/src/syscall/socketpair.rs:51, carries the identical catch-all and returns EAFNOSUPPORT for every non-AF_UNIX family; host measures EOPNOTSUPP(95) for socketpair(AF_INET, SOCK_STREAM|SOCK_DGRAM, 0) and EPROTONOSUPPORT(93) for socketpair(AF_INET, SOCK_RAW, 0), so it is wrong two different ways. It also parses Protocol::try_from at line 25 and then never inspects the value, so socketpair(AF_UNIX, SOCK_STREAM, 6) succeeds where the host returns EPROTONOSUPPORT. socketpair01 is in the same all.txt pool and lands on exactly this. (2) The four netlink arms, socket.rs:74-86, return EAFNOSUPPORT for unsupported, user-range and invalid netlink families; the host returns EPROTONOSUPPORT(93) for all of protocol 3, 31, 40 and -1 on AF_NETLINK, so every one is wrong, on a family Asterinas otherwise fully supports. AF_NETLINK+SOCK_STREAM additionally falls to line 93's EAFNOSUPPORT where the host returns ESOCKTNOSUPPORT(94). (3) Any recognised family with an unhandled type -- AF_INET+SOCK_RDM/SOCK_DCCP, AF_VSOCK+SOCK_DGRAM -- reaches line 93 and reports EAFNOSUPPORT; the host returns ESOCKTNOSUPPORT for AF_INET+SOCK_RDM. (4) Protocol::try_from at lines 39 and 54 maps every protocol number with no Protocol enum variant to EINVAL via error.rs:348-352, but the host returns EPROTONOSUPPORT for an in-range unassigned protocol (99 measured) and EINVAL only for out-of-range values (300 and -1 measured, Linux gates on IPPROTO_MAX=256). socket01 does not reach this: its protocols are 0, 1, 6 and 17, all of which are enum variants. (5) The AF_UNIX arms at lines 29-37 never look at protocol at all, so socket(AF_UNIX, SOCK_STREAM, 6) succeeds where the host returns EPROTONOSUPPORT. Separately, SockFlags::from_bits_truncate at line 21 silently discards unknown flag bits where the host returns EINVAL. Explicitly NOT this bug: AF_INET6+SOCK_DGRAM has no arm at all (line 53 is AF_INET-only) so it reaches line 93, but the host creates a UDPv6 socket there -- that is a missing IPv6-datagram feature, not an errno defect, and it is out of scope.
suggested_direction: Smallest change that satisfies the invariant on the four failing rows: at socket.rs:50 and :60 replace Errno::EAFNOSUPPORT with Errno::EPROTONOSUPPORT (the messages already read 'unsupported protocol', so only the constant is wrong) -- this fixes tdat[5], tdat[6] and tdat[8]; and add an explicit (CSocketAddrFamily::AF_INET | CSocketAddrFamily::AF_INET6, SockType::SOCK_RAW) arm returning EPROTONOSUPPORT -- this fixes tdat[3]. The added arm is defensible beyond the test: it matches the host exactly for protocol 0, and since Asterinas implements no raw IP protocol at all, EPROTONOSUPPORT is the honest answer for the other protocols too (the host would succeed for protocol 1 and 255 as root, but that needs raw-socket support, a separate missing feature). Do not use EPERM -- the host returns EPROTONOSUPPORT even with full capabilities. Critical trap, and the reason this is not a one-line errno swap: line 93's catch-all must keep returning EAFNOSUPPORT. CSocketAddrFamily::AF_UNSPEC = 0 is a real enum variant (kernel/src/util/net/addr/family.rs:22), so CSocketAddrFamily::try_from(0) succeeds for tdat[0] and the EAFNOSUPPORT that makes that row pass today comes from line 93, not from try_from. Flipping the catch-all's errno to make tdat[3] pass would turn tdat[0] red and keep the score at 5/9. Beyond the minimum, and preferred if the fix is to sit at the owning layer: hoist the family x type x protocol table out of sys_socket into a shared family dispatch under kernel/src/net/socket/ that sys_socketpair also calls, so socketpair stops carrying a divergent copy; give recognised-family/unhandled-type its own ESOCKTNOSUPPORT arm instead of falling through to the domain catch-all; and switch the netlink arms at 74-86 to EPROTONOSUPPORT. Those extras are not required to turn socket01 green and can be scoped out, but the fix should at least not entrench the conflation.
